_meta.goal: Money flow to each district over time + who is responsible + how the system functions/dysfunctions. Pilot district: Kolkata.
_meta.rules: PDF-cited or it's a gap. Every fact carries source + source_tier. Gaps recorded in _gaps, never guessed. Footnotes in UI point to the public record.
_meta.footnotes_render: source_tier 4 (news) and 3 (wikipedia) are shown but visibly flagged as needing upgrade to a government PDF source.

coverage.note: Kolkata: KMC civic budget grant flow now TIER-1 PDF-cited (₹2,897 cr Govt Grant of ₹5,525 cr receipts, BE 2025-26). MPLADS spent/completed figures tier-4 (2026-01-06 review) pending upgrade to official MPLADS portal. Roster partially sourced.

system_notes.note: Kolkata has no conventional District Magistrate/Collector. Magisterial powers vest in the Commissioner of Police (one of the oldest such posts in British India); a limited Collector post handles stamp revenue/registration; service delivery is run by the Kolkata Municipal Corporation. A standard 'who is the DM responsible for this money' question therefore has no single answer here.

MPLADS delivery in Kolkata's metro seats is recommendation-heavy but completion-poor: Kolkata Uttar completed 3 of 36 works, Kolkata Dakshin 0 of 73 (as on 2026-01-06). A WB-wide review found dense metropolitan seats show limited tangible outcomes versus rural constituencies — money flows in on paper but converts to far less on the ground.

Fiscal dependence: ~52% of Kolkata Municipal Corporation's ₹5,525 cr receipts (BE 2025-26) is Government Grant-in-Aid from Central + State governments (₹2,897 cr), versus ₹2,628 cr raised from its own sources. More than half of the city's civic money is transferred down rather than locally generated — and the budget still runs a deficit (expenditure ₹5,639.56 cr).

ledger.scheme: KMC civic budget — Government Grant (Central + State Grant-in-Aid)
ledger.money_in_basis: Budget Estimate 2025-26 'Government Grant' line; explicitly Grant-in-Aids from both Central and State Governments. (RE 2024-25: ₹2,347 cr.)
ledger.intended: Civic services: water supply, solid waste, sewerage & drainage, roads, slum development, health, lighting, education.

what_happened.notes: Government grant of ₹2,897 cr is ~52% of KMC's ₹5,525 cr total receipts — over half of Kolkata's civic money flows DOWN from Central+State govt, not raised locally. Budget is in deficit (expenditure ₹5,639.56 cr > receipts ₹5,524.84 cr). Named schemes flowing through: 15th Finance Commission Health Grants, AMRUT 2.0, NMCG (river/canal cleaning), NSAP, DAY-NULM.

ledger.through_dept: Kolkata Uttar — released via nodal District Authority
ledger.money_in_basis: entitlement: ~₹10 cr cumulative (₹5 cr/yr × ~2 FY into 18th LS)
ledger.intended: MP recommends local works; District Authority sanctions/executes/pays vendors.

what_happened.notes: Only 3 of 36 recommended works completed; ₹2.25 cr spent of ~₹10 cr entitlement. Money was recommended and partly disbursed but tangible delivery is low — a 'recommended ≠ spent ≠ completed' gap.

ledger.through_dept: Kolkata Dakshin — released via nodal District Authority
ledger.money_in_basis: entitlement: ~₹10 cr cumulative (₹5 cr/yr × ~2 FY into 18th LS)
ledger.intended: MP recommends local works; District Authority sanctions/executes/pays vendors.

what_happened.notes: 73 works recommended, ZERO completed; ₹2.74 cr spent of ~₹10 cr. Highest recommendation count among the three Kolkata-area seats, lowest completion. Stark 'money wasn't spent right' case.
